text:
Connor Hellebuyck's season started with a standoff. The 2025 Hart Trophy winner didn't report to Winnipeg's training camp, the Jets suspended him, and on Oct. 23 they traded him to New Jersey, as the Associated Press reported. He then sat out the Devils' visit to Winnipeg last week, a decision the Jets' coach criticized.

On the ice, none of the drama shows. He's 7-0-0 as a Devil with a .916 save percentage and 2.5 goals saved above expected (goals stopped beyond what the shots were worth), and NHL.com has the Devils rising in the Metropolitan Division with the trade as a boost. His rebound control is the best part of the profile: only 8.0% of his saves lead to another shot within three seconds, against a league 10.8%.

The caveats are real. Seven games is a small sample, and high-danger shots have beaten him a little more than average (.667 against a league .685). Last season was quieter than his reputation by our numbers, plus 3.4 in 57 games, though Evolving-Hockey's model rated it far higher. A three-time Vezina winner gets a long leash, and he starts tonight against Montreal.
